commitResults.messageBody:
Add a fixed-size array (String[100]) to store tasks so the "list"
command can echo them back, per the requirement that no more than
100 tasks need to be supported. Guards against blank input being
stored (which previously broke list's null-check termination) and
against exceeding the array's capacity.

commitResults.messageTitle: docs: note that commands are case-sensitive
commitResults.messageBody:
Clarify in the user guide that command matching is exact-case, since
the underlying implementation compares input strings directly (e.g.
"List" is not recognized as "list").

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: add Task class and mark/unmark commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce a Task class (description + done state) to replace the
String[] task list, so each task can carry its own status. Add
mark/unmark commands that parse a 1-indexed task number and flip its
done state, with bounds checking so an out-of-range or non-numeric
index reports an error instead of crashing.

list now iterates up to taskCount instead of scanning the full
100-slot array for a null sentinel, and the input line is trimmed
once up front so exit-command matching and word-splitting agree on
what counts as the command (previously trailing whitespace could
bypass the exit check while still being treated as a task by mistake).

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: split Nia into Ui/TaskList, flatten command handling with guard clauses
commitResults.messageBody:
refactor: split Nia into Ui/TaskList, flatten command handling

Command dispatch in main() nested up to 6 levels deep (switch -> case ->
if -> try/catch -> if), making it hard to follow. Extracted:
- Ui: all user-facing output (banners, bars, personality lines, indenting)
- TaskList: owns the task array + count instead of main() juggling both
- Nia: main() now only reads input and dispatches; each command is its
  own handleXxx() method using guard clauses instead of nested ifs

Also restyles input/reply wrapping (bars now frame the user's input line
instead of Nia's reply) and adds Javadoc to Task/Nia; see designer_log.txt

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: split input/parsing/logic/output into dedicated classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Nia.main previously mixed reading input, sanitizing it, dispatching
commands, and printing. Ui.java mixed personality voicelines with
generic output formatting. Split into:
- InputReader: raw stdin reads only
- Parser: sanitizes input into canonical words, owns command-alias
  resolution (bye/close/exit/quit -> bye), single place to add
  future aliases (e.g. dl -> deadline)
- Processor: pure command dispatch on canonical words, no
  sanitization or alias knowledge
- Printer: generic terminal output (replaces formatting half of Ui)
- VoicelineManager: personality content, prints via Printer
  (replaces personality half of Ui)

Nia.main now only orchestrates the read -> parse -> process loop.
See designer_log.txt entry 4 for full rationale.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: add Todo/Deadline/Event task types with dedicated command parsing
commitResults.messageBody:
Task is now a common supertype rather than something instantiated
directly; Todo/Deadline/Event each override getTag()/toString() to add
their own tag and fields. Parser resolves td/dl aliases and splits
input into the command-specific shape each type needs (todo:
[cmd, description]; deadline: [cmd, description, by] split on "/by";
event: [cmd, description, from, to] split on "/from"/"/to"), leaving
missing fields as empty strings for Processor to validate. Processor
now rejects unrecognized commands instead of silently turning them
into tasks, and list output uses each task's toString() so the type
tag and extra fields show up.
